verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately extract all 41 prepaid expense invoices and 25 prepaid insurance invoices, properly apply the 6-month default and specific insurance coverage periods, and reconcile to the provided GL balances through April 2025. Deliverable A is stronger because it goes several steps further in creating a complete, senior-level accounting workbook. First, Deliverable A includes a full 'YTD Amortization Expense by GL Account (Jan - Apr 2025)' table on the summary tab (rows 33-43) and includes both the Expense GL # and Expense Account Name on the detail tabs, whereas Deliverable B only lists the Expense Acct # column without the account name or a GL expense summary table. Second, Deliverable A extends the amortization schedules through the full service period of the recorded invoices (clearly separating 'Actual' Jan-Apr columns from 'Projected' May-Sep/Dec columns), while Deliverable B stops its schedule columns at April 2025. Finally, Deliverable A avoids adding redundant single-line vendor subtotals (like 'Subtotal - ALTAIR' and 'Subtotal - AMESITE' in Deliverable B) when a vendor only has one invoice, making the schedule cleaner to read.

decisive_issues.issue: Schedule columns stop at April 2025 rather than showing the full amortization period of the recorded invoices, and lacks an Expense GL Account summary table or Account Name column.
Adds redundant vendor subtotal rows even for vendors with only a single invoice.
